Own digest: Paper card. Question: Can high-entropy solid solutions be formed in non-oxide ceramic metal diborides with a hexagonal layered structure, and do they exhibit superior hardness and oxidation resistance compared to their constituent individual diborides?. System: Seven equimolar five-component metal diborides: (Hf0.2Zr0.2Ta0.2Nb0.2Ti0.2)B2, (Hf0.2Zr0.2Ta0.2Mo0.2Ti0.2)B2, (Hf0.2Zr0.2Mo0.2Nb0.2Ti0.2)B2, (Hf0.2Mo0.2Ta0.2Nb0.2Ti0.2)B2, (Mo0.2Zr0.2Ta0.2Nb0.2Ti0.2)B2, (Hf0.2Zr0.2Ta0.2Cr0.2Ti0.2)B2, and (Hf0.2Zr0.2W0.2Mo0.2Ti0.2)B2. Processing: High-energy ball milling (HEBM) for 6 hours in WC media with 60-minute milling/5-minute cooling cycles, followed by spark plasma sintering (SPS) at 2000 °C for 5 minutes under 30 MPa pressure in vacuum (10^-2 Torr). Test conditions: Hardness measured via Vickers indentation at 200 kgf/mm2 with 15s hold time; oxidation resistance assessed via sequential isothermal annealing in flowing dry air at 800–1500 °C for 1 h
